issues.description: Equal-rank terminal states overwrite each other without recency checks, so an older COMPLETED dump can replace a newer FAILED result.
Unchanged detection compares only state, end, and elapsed_sec, so corrected user, partition, submit/start, CPU, GPU, or exit_code values are ignored.
job_id is the only primary key, which can merge unrelated jobs if data spans clusters, accounting sources, or Slurm job ID reuse.
AllocCPUS, user, partition, and exit_code are not range/content validated, allowing empty identity fields and negative CPU usage into reports.
GPU counts are parsed with int() but never checked for non-negative values, allowing negative GPU-hours.
ISO timestamps are compared as text, which gives incorrect chronological filtering and top-window behavior when timezone offsets are present.
Rows with submit, start, and end all missing are accepted even though reports silently exclude them from time-window queries.
A database containing only records with NULL reference times is reported as empty by top_users().
Report commands use the same connect path that creates new databases, so a typo in --db silently creates an empty DB instead of failing.
The SQLite directory and file are created with default umask-derived permissions, which may expose user/job accounting data on shared systems.
The schema has no user_version or migration path, so future schema changes can leave existing databases silently incompatible.
State-transition tests cover terminal-vs-running downgrades but miss terminal-to-terminal stale overwrite regressions.
